story.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang

facts.text: Nvidia's Board of Directors is preparing to oust co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang following revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence and another with an Nvidia executive , reports The Wall Street Journal .
Although no final decision has been made yet, the company's directors could meet as early as November 11 to discuss Huang's future.
Nvidia's stock dropped 8% in after-hours trading following the reports.

Huang's potential departure would mark the first CEO transition in Nvidia's 33-year history, and therefore his succession has become an immediate concern for Nvidia, which does not have anyone of Huang's caliber in the leadership team.
However, has not served in an executive role at Nvidia for at least a decade, so the chances that he will succeed Huang are low.

The report from the WSJ comes hours after the New York Times revealed that Huang allegedly had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports directly to him.
According to five people who worked at Nvidia, the relationship was known internally, while Huang and Powell were reportedly seen together at a San Jose hotel during Nvidia's GTC conference in March.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware.
Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.
Back on Sunday, directors expressed confidence in Jensen Huang and his leadership team, a choice of words that did not exactly guarantee his continued tenure.

Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang and could meet as soon as Wednesday, the Wall Street Journal reported, after the Times reported his relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell; Nvidia fell 7.4% after hours to $160.95 (6:30 PM ET).

That came three days after Huang told employees he had been unfaithful to his wife, following reports that linked him to Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore's Megaspeed whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China.
China calls that claim groundless, and Huang has not been accused of a crime.
The first-day drops were small in both cases, under 3%.
Nvidia has already fallen more than that after hours tonight alone.
What separated the two outcomes came later, and it was mostly about two things: whether the board had a successor ready on day one, and whether the business underneath was healthy.
Intel had neither, and its stock lagged for the year that followed.
Huang being removed immediately could be challenging for Nvidia since it does not have a succession plan in place," Gil Luria of D.A.
Davidson told Reuters after the Journal's report.
Huang co-founded the company in 1993 and has run it ever since, which makes him harder to replace than Krzanich or Easterbrook, who were both hired managers.
Baird analysts Tristan Gerra and Tyler Bomba wrote earlier Wednesday that a CEO change was growing more likely and that an outside hire would be favored.
Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives has said Nvidia would be worth 25% to 30% less without Huang.
On the other side, Nvidia's business is far healthier than Intel's was in 2018, and a Blind survey found 88% of 232 Nvidia employees want Huang to stay.
For a holder with $100,000 in Nvidia, about 621 shares at the after-hours price, the two histories frame the range.
Neither history includes a founder, so the real range is probably wider in both directions.
A relationship with a direct report turns the board's problem into one that boards have handled before, and twice in the past decade the CEO had to go.
Here is what happened to shareholders those two times.
On Sunday, November 3, 2019, McDonald's said its board had fired CEO Steve Easterbrook for a consensual relationship with an employee, which violated company policy.
In August 2020 the company sued Easterbrook, saying he had hidden other relationships, and in 2021 he agreed to return more than $105 million in pay.

Chief financial officer Bob Swan ran the company as interim CEO for seven months before the board gave him the job in January 2019, while Intel was also struggling to get its next generation of chips into production.
A fast, credible choice was the difference between the two cases above.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
McDonald's stock fell 2.7% the next trading day.
A year later, with dividends counted, it was up 14.7%, ahead of the S&P 500's 11.9%, even with the 2020 crash in between.
Six months in, during that crash, both McDonald's and the index were down: 7.6% and 6.1%.
Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports .
Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company.
The stock is down about 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said .
The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, gives a keynote address on October 21 in Berlin.

(CNN) — Nvidia shares dropped sharply in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with a company executive and that the board is meeting to discuss his future.
The drop in Nvidia shares weighed on the broader market: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.1% and S&P 500 futures fell 0.5% as of 6:30 p.m ET.
Huang on Sunday apologized for an extramarital affair, although he did not name the other party.
Investors are weighing the outlook for the chipmaker that’s been at the center of the AI boom if Huang is ousted from his role.
The CEO has been one of AI’s most steadfast cheerleaders and funders, and investors have flocked to Nvidia shares because of his vision for the tech boom.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment about the new reports.
